title: Upper/mid/lower thoracic flexion ROM at max flexion and with neutral vs flexed lumbar spine (standing)
condition: healthy, standing, maximal flexion and combined lumbar/thoracic flexion postures

quantity.name: regional thoracic flexion ROM
quantity.definition: sagittal angle change between proximal and distal marker plates of each region, upright to held posture

source.sample: 13 males; 13 right-handed males free of neck, back and shoulder pain for >= 1 year (university population)

protocol.summary: At max forward flexion thoracic flexion is concentrated in T9-T12 (35 deg) vs T5-T8 (12) and T1-T4 (4); lower thoracic flexion grows with lumbar flexion.
how_to_use: For full standing forward flexion allocate thoracic flexion ≈ 69% to T9-T12, 23% to T5-T8, 8% to T1-T4 (35.3/11.8/4.3 deg).
For thoracic 'slump' (chin to chest) with neutral lumbar spine use a more even split (~9-15 deg per region).
Skin-plate regional angles; lower-thoracic value may include some thoracolumbar motion.

measurement.device: Vicon MX 50 Hz; rigid 3-marker plates on spinous processes defining T1-T4, T5-T8, T9-T12 and L1-PSIS segments; regional angle between proximal and distal plates
measurement.task: max forward flexion; max right axial twist; ~50% lumbar flexion or neutral lumbar combined with thoracic flexion (chin to chest) or right thoracic twist; 5 s hold

extraction.from: Results text (6 of 9 means with SD); Fig 2 (lumbar-neutral thoracic-flexed bars)
extraction.uncertainty: text values as printed; digitised values ±0.2 deg (mean) and ±0.2 deg (SD)
extraction.check_notes: Fig 2 calibrated on the 6 text values (bar tops reproduce them within 0.08 deg, SD whiskers within 0.13 deg) before reading the 3 lumbar-neutral thoracic-flexed bars.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
